chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Isa al-Uraydi, Abu Muhammad, who said:

When Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) passed away, a man from the people of Egypt came to Makkah with wealth for the Nāḥiyah. Disagreement arose over it, so some people said: “Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) passed away without a successor, and the successor is Jaʿfar,” while others said: “Abu Muhammad passed away leaving a successor.”
So he sent a man whose kunyah was Abu Talib. He arrived at al-ʿAskar carrying a letter, then went to Jaʿfar and asked him for a proof, and he said: “That is not possible at this time.”

Then he went to the door and delivered the letter to our companions, and there came out to him: “May Allah reward you concerning your companion, for he has died. He entrusted the wealth that was with him to a trustworthy person so that he may act regarding it as is required, and his letter has been answered.”

key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ: Abu Muhammad, Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (عليه السلام)
key_terms.النَّاحِيَةِ: the sacred authority or designated side, referring here to the Imam’s office
key_terms.الْعَسْكَرَ: al-ʿAskar, the locality associated with Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (عليه السلام)
key_terms.الْمَالِ: the wealth or funds being delivered
key_terms.بُرْهَانٍ: proof or decisive evidence of rightful authority
key_terms.ثِقَةٍ: a trustworthy person entrusted with responsibility
key_terms.خَلَفٍ: successor who comes after the Imam

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the dispute over the successor after Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) and the delivery of wealth to the Nāḥiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an incident after the passing of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (عليه السلام), when dispute arose concerning the rightful successor and the handling of entrusted wealth. The report presents recognition of the hidden successor through a divinely guided response and proper direction regarding the entrusted funds.
